editorial:
Ever wonder why some of the simplest things in your house are actually genius? You get to hang out with the witty Stephen Fry as he counts down the top 100 gadgets that changed the world. It feels less like a dry history lesson and more like a chat with a very smart friend who is obsessed with how things work. From basic tools like the tin opener to high-tech gear like the iPod, the vibe is light, curious, and genuinely fun. You will find yourself looking at your own kitchen drawers differently after seeing how much thought went into these inventions.

What really works here is the fast pacing and Fry's natural charm. He keeps you interested even when talking about boring-sounding items like trouser presses. The only downside is that it moves so quickly you might wish he spent more time on a few specific items. If you love trivia or just like seeing cool machines, you need to see this. It looks great if you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but it is also a great pick to add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for a permanent home library.
endingExplained: As the countdown hits the top spots, Fry focuses on the gadgets that truly shifted human history. He wraps things up by reflecting on how small ideas lead to massive changes in how we live. The final scenes highlight the most impactful inventions, ending with a thoughtful look at the balance between simple tools and complex tech. It finishes on a high note, leaving you feeling amazed at human creativity and the tools we take for granted.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves trivia, history, and cool inventions.
